clue.text: Station sailors in the ship — they'll keep things secure

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for a plural noun

parts.note: to station something is to set or place it

indicators.note: the sailors are placed inside the ship, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: SS, steamship, wraps around the sailors
a ship's sailors are its crew

explanation.surface: A naval post: the sailors are stationed aboard and are the ones who keep things safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The sailors sound like the ones keeping things secure, but the closing clause describes small engineering fasteners.
explanation.definitionFit: Set screws are threaded fasteners driven in to hold a part firmly in position on a shaft.

clue.text: This runs on water — beats atom smashing!

indicators.note: smashing breaks things into pieces, so the letters before it are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A boast that a water-powered engine outdoes nuclear fission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs on water' sounds like fuel; it means travels on the water's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamboat is a vessel driven by a steam engine that plies rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Open up with evident hesitation and come to the point

parts.note: to tap a barrel is to open it
er is the sound of audible hesitation

explanation.surface: A shy speaker opens up haltingly before getting to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come to the point' sounds like getting to the gist; it means narrowing to a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to narrow gradually towards one end until it forms a tip.

clue.text: Stupid — unlike The Times crossword solver

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lacking any idea or sense

definitions.note: a cryptic description: someone with no clues
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: without clues, which a solver of this puzzle certainly has

explanation.walkthrough: It seems a jibe at the solver; in fact the solver is the one person who has clues in front of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has no idea at all is said to be without a clue, an everyday idiom.

clue.text: Stop with some exasperation when put in jeopardy

parts.note: to end is to stop
anger is a degree of exasperation

explanation.surface: Someone halts in irritation on finding things at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to expose someone or something to harm or risk.

clue.text: Taking a gun to church makes no appeal to sense

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for a noun

parts.note: the Sten was a British submachine gun
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Carrying a weapon into a church is not a sensible move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sense' looks like good judgement; it is the sense of smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a foul smell, something that offends the nose rather than pleasing it.

clue.text: A rapid writer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Irish satirist who wrote Gulliver's Travels

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one person, a fast writer, but the adjective and the noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift means quick, and Jonathan Swift was the eighteenth-century author of Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: A scholar's holding motorists up, being a crawler

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top
holding something keeps it inside, so the motorists sit within the scholar's letters

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a scholar; the apostrophe-s adds S
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A clever student is causing a traffic jam, and is a creep about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawler' suggests a sycophant; it is a beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarab is a dung beetle, an insect that creeps along the ground, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Reforming can tire — it can get complicated

indicators.note: reforming something gives it a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: seven letters of the fodder
the last two letters of the fodder

explanation.surface: A weary comment that reform is exhausting and gets messy.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate means having many interconnected parts or details, and so hard to follow.

clue.text: Few engineers are articled

indicators.note: to be articled here is to be set inside an article, a word such as 'the'

parts.note: 'the' is the definite article
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Only a handful of engineers have served formal apprenticeships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articled' sounds like a trainee contract; it means put in an article.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is a small number, so it can stand in for a few, a loose crossword sense.

clue.text: Say something about former currency

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
the pound is Britain's currency

explanation.surface: Someone holding forth about money that is no longer in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former currency' looks like one obsolete coin; it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to set out or explain a topic at length, speaking in detail on it.

clue.text: "Rubbish! Many cut back.", he claims

definitions.note: a clause standing for a noun: one who claims

indicators.note: going back means the assembled string is read from right to left

parts.note: rot is nonsense
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing complaints about heavy cuts as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it sound like a speech; the definition is the speaker, 'he claims', i.e. one who demands.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is a person who demands or extorts payment, insisting on what is owed as a right.

clue.text: Additional cash required for mushroom production

parts.note: additional means more
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin librae

explanation.surface: Extra funding is needed to grow mushrooms commercially.
explanation.definitionFit: The morel is an edible wild fungus with a honeycombed cap, prized in cooking.

clue.text: Fruit drink fit for the gods in the Orient

parts.note: nectar was the drink of the Greek gods
taken as written
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A heavenly juice served somewhere in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a stone fruit.

clue.text: Viewed too much, so must be supervised

definitions.meaning: second meaning: watched over in charge

explanation.surface: A child who watches too much television needs supervising.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is a coinage: 'over' plus 'seen', seen too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise, and its past participle is the same word read as seen excessively.

clue.text: "By -— most have been misled" (Dryden)

parts.note: surface reading: a quotation with a missing word
setter's reading: the poet John Dryden's line from The Hind and the Panther, blaming upbringing for false beliefs

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the solver supplies the missing word from Dryden's line about how people come by mistaken beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryden's couplet runs 'By education most have been misled; So they believe, because they so were bred.'

clue.text: Mean to grab one or two

indicators.note: grabbing takes something into one's hold, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: par is the average or norm
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A stingy person reaching for one or two items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' suggests stingy; here it is the average, as in par for the course.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a set of two matching things, such as two socks or two people.

clue.text: Reviving with eau-de-Cologne say after near-collapse

indicators.note: a collapse leaves things in a heap, so the letters of the word before it fall into a new order
after places the perfume piece at the end of the answer

parts.note: four letters rearranged
eau de Cologne is an example of a scent

explanation.surface: Bringing someone round with cologne after they nearly fainted.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn or coming back to life, rising again after decline.

clue.text: Returns concerned with equipment

parts.note: re means about or concerning
stores are supplies and equipment

explanation.surface: A shop's goods coming back, or a department dealing with kit.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to give it back or return it to its former state.

clue.text: Resplendent silver bedding

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
litter is straw bedding for animals

explanation.surface: Luxurious silver bed linen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bedding' suggests sheets; it is the straw laid down for livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglitter means sparkling or shining brightly, as something resplendent does.

clue.text: Tense abstemious fellow with a heart of gold

indicators.note: a heart sits in the middle, so the fellow's letters surround it

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes one who abstains from drink
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A nervous, sober man who is kind at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut means stretched tight, and so strained or tense, of rope or of nerves.

clue.text: The colour of those suffering from mal-de-mer?

definitions.text: The colour of those suffering from mal-de-mer?

parts.words: The colour of those suffering from mal-de-mer?
parts.note: surface reading: a medical question about seasick passengers' complexion

parts.words: The colour of those suffering from mal-de-mer?
parts.note: setter's reading: queasy sailors go a pale shade, and they are at sea when it happens

explanation.walkthrough: Mal de mer is French for seasickness; people feeling sick are said to turn green.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea green is a pale bluish-green shade, named for the colour of sea water.

clue.text: Best of French achievement

definitions.note: verb: to get the better of

indicators.note: French tells the solver to translate the little word into that language

parts.note: de is French for of
a feat is an achievement

explanation.surface: Praise for the greatest of French accomplishments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective; it is the verb, to overcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To best an opponent is to beat or defeat them in a contest.

clue.text: A trying man upset better-half

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word after it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the word upset split as up plus set; only the set part supplies letters

indicators.note: keeping only half of a word throws away the other half

parts.note: taken as written, before halving

explanation.surface: A tiresome husband has annoyed his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits 'upset' into 'up' (reverse, in a down light) and 'set', and takes the back half of 'better'; 'better half' looks like a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is someone who tries things out, trial being a sense of trying.

clue.text: Appallingly mean beast bringing disgrace

indicators.note: something done appallingly is done terribly badly, so the letters fall into disorder

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A horribly cruel animal bringing shame on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is humiliation, the state of being lowered in dignity or esteem.

clue.text: Jack is on edge, unable to take any more

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB is an able seaman
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A nervous man named Jack has had enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' looks like nervous; the edge piece follows the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrim means full to the brim, so a vessel that is abrim cannot hold anything further.

clue.text: Clubs with uplifting aims

parts.note: surface reading: societies with inspiring or improving goals
setter's reading: golf clubs with lofted faces, designed to lift the ball into the air

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' suggests morally improving; in golf these angled clubs are meant to get the ball airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are golf clubs with metal heads and angled faces, numbered by how much loft they give.

clue.text: A little springbok — a picturesque animal

indicators.note: only a little of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: letters running across the end of the first word and into the next two

explanation.surface: A small antelope makes a pretty creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The springbok is an African antelope, which steers you toward another African beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest animal of central Africa, a short-necked relative of the giraffe.

clue.text: The intention in regular payment for clothes

indicators.note: the intention is put inside the payment, so one word sits within another

parts.note: rent is paid regularly for a home
an aim is an intention

explanation.surface: Someone's purpose in a regular allowance is to buy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing or garments.

clue.text: Run over? Right, create commotion!

indicators.note: a commotion is a disturbance, so the letters next to it are thrown about

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
the six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver who hits someone, then sees the chance to make a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run over' suggests a road accident; it means going over the same ground again.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrace one's steps or a route is to go back over it a second time.

clue.text: The painter Doctor X backed

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer

indicators.note: something backed has gone backwards, so the number is read from right to left

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: An artist supported by a mysterious Doctor X.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter of the Water Lilies series.

clue.text: Leisure should include exercise to develop self-control

indicators.note: including something takes it inside, so the leisure word goes around the other

parts.note: rest is leisure time
to train is to exercise in order to develop skill or strength

explanation.surface: Advice that time off should involve working out to build discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is holding oneself back, the exercise of self-discipline or moderation.
